name: Civil unrest
summary: France's weekly living-cost protests shrink from 320,000 on 31 Oct to 106,000 on 14 Nov; no deadly nationwide unrest
state: France's interior ministry counted 320,000 living-cost protesters nationwide on 31 Oct, down from 550,000 on 17 Oct (Reuters via Devdiscourse), and about 106,000 on 14 Nov, the fifth weekend, when police used tear gas in Paris, Bordeaux and Nantes (Türkiye Today). Turnout has kept falling since. Significant protests keep Watch, trending down; searches on 28 Nov found no deadly nationwide unrest or state crackdown in a major country.
for_you: People travelling in or through France may meet marches and transport strikes at weekends. FCDO travel advice lists current demonstrations and their effect on travel.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests (France, 106,000 on 14 Nov); no deadly nationwide unrest in a major country

sources.title: Türkiye Today — France's weekend rallies draw 106,000 by official count while unions claim 200,000
Devdiscourse (Reuters) — Turnout for French protests lower than during previous Saturdays, interior ministry says

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
